offence_severity: Death caused by causing grievous hurt (section 302) - minimum 10 years, maximum death sentence
physical_harm: Third degree burns over 90% of the body and an incised wound on the back
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation/planning as they were waiting in ambush and prepared with weapons
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the dying declarations (statements Ext. P-20 and P-17) and the testimony of the eye witness PW13 as key evidence, which consistently named the respondents and described their role in surrounding the deceased and preventing his escape.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, including PW13, as credible eye witnesses whose testimony was corroborated by the post-mortem report, indicating their presence and active participation in the crime.

appeal_history.supreme_court: Set aside the acquittal and restored the conviction

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the deceased was caught by the accused, petrol was poured over him, and fire was lit. The deceased ran, was surrounded by the respondents, and attacked with a sword and burning tyre. The trial court convicted all the accused, and the High Court's acquittal was challenged.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the respondents arrived at the scene after the commission of the offence and that the charge of formation of an unlawful assembly was not established.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the role of the respondents in the commission of the crime was clearly established by the dying declaration and eye witness testimony, indicating their active participation and intent.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the respondents were found to have participated in the crime, acted in concert, and ensured the deceased could not escape, thereby fulfilling the elements of the offence under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Penal Code.
